Meet your grammar guides!

Every great story needs both tenses. Memo teaches the imperfect; Solo teaches the preterite. Both cats can appear in sentences using either tense.

🐱 Memo — El imperfecto

Sets the scene

Era una tarde tranquila.It was a quiet afternoon.

Hacía mucho sol.It was very sunny.

Memo dormía debajo de un árbol.Memo was sleeping under a tree.

Solo tenía hambre.Solo was hungry.

What was going on? What were things like? What did people use to do?

🐈 Solo — El pretérito

Moves the story forward

De repente, apareció una mariposa.Suddenly, a butterfly appeared.

Memo abrió los ojos.Memo opened his eyes.

Solo corrió hacia la mariposa.Solo ran toward the butterfly.

La mariposa desapareció.The butterfly disappeared.

What happened? What happened next? How did the experience go?

✏️ Write this in your notes
  • Imperfect: sets the scene — background, habits, conditions and ongoing actions.
  • Preterite: moves the story forward — completed events and bounded experiences.
Both work together to tell a story.

Two ways to view the past

Storytelling is our starting point. Perspective explains why both tenses can describe the same condition.

🐱 MEMO · IMPERFECTO

Sets the scene

Inside the experienceMemo dormía.Memo was sleeping.

We see the sleeping in progress. Its endpoints are not the focus.

🐈 SOLO · PRETÉRITO

Moves the story forward

The experience as a wholeMemo durmió.Memo slept.

We view the sleeping as a completed event.

✏️ Write this in your notes
Imperfect: What was going on? What were things like?
Preterite: What happened? How did the experience go?
Both can describe long or short experiences. The speaker’s perspective matters.

Why perspective matters

🐱 Inside the experience

Estaba cansado cuando llegué al hotel.I was tired when I arrived at the hotel.

Imagine a snapshot during a vacation. We describe the condition at that moment; its endpoints are not the focus.

🐈 The experience as a whole

Estuve cansado durante todo el viaje.I was tired throughout the trip.

Imagine looking back on the completed vacation. We summarize a bounded experience. This does not necessarily mean the tiredness stopped immediately afterward.

Remember: Weather and feelings can use either tense. Long events can use the preterite, and exciting actions can use the imperfect.

Un monstruo perseguía a Memo mientras Solo gritaba.A monster was chasing Memo while Solo was screaming.

Exciting, but already in progress.

De repente, Memo encontró una puerta y escapó.Suddenly, Memo found a door and escaped.

These events move the story forward.

Una noche inesperada

An unexpected night
